parts.name: gibbon
sources: MakeHuman (CC0): the low-poly body male1591, the skeleton game_engine and its weights (https://github.com/makehumancommunity/mpfb2); the head of a macaque and the tail are of World. CC0 1.0 (public domain): https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

A northern white-cheeked gibbon (vượn đen má trắng, Nomascus leucogenys), a male: about 55 cm long, no tail, very long arms, black with white cheeks. On the ground it walks on two legs with the arms up.

Wikipedia, Northern white-cheeked gibbon (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_white-cheeked_gibbon): "both males and females have unusually long arms, even for gibbons", the arms 1.2 to 1.4 times the legs; "Males have black hair over their entire bodies, except for distinct white patches on their cheeks"; "an average weight of 7.5 kg".
Animal Diversity Web, Nomascus leucogenys (https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Nomascus_leucogenys): 45 to 63 cm long.
Wikipedia, Gibbon (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibbon): "Like all of the apes, gibbons are tailless." They "walk bipedally with their arms raised for balance".

The template of primates has a tail: the gibbon has the shortest tail of the numbers (0.1), thin. The arms 1.55 and the legs 0.72 of the template, which has arms 0.61 times its legs: the arms 1.3 times the legs. A guess from photos of iNaturalist.
The lengths of the fur (fur): a guess from photos of the animal, not a measurement.
